title: GPU pool fallbacks & circuit breaker notes (post-incident draft)
content:
Context:
During the 2025-11-06 evening window we observed a progressive degradation of one Dedicated GPU pool (pool-id: pool-west-01) that manifested as elevated 95th/99th latency and a growing queue of pending requests. Autoscaler did expand the pool, but due to a set of related failures the system did not fail over traffic gracefully and some customer routes saw sustained latency > 5s for ~47 minutes. This doc is a working post-incident capture + runbook draft for adding explicit circuit-breaker and fallback behavior for pool-level degradation.
content_continued:
High-level timeline (abridged):
- 2025-11-06 18:03 UTC: first alerts from per-pool latency SLO (alert: pool-latency-95 > 2s for 3m).
- 18:05 UTC: probing synthetic jobs show rising kernel preemption counts and occasional CUDA memcopy stalls on nodes in pool-west-01.
- 18:09 UTC: autoscaler triggered expansion + reschedule; new nodes booted but kube-scheduler backoff due to imagePullRateLimit on some nodes (partial).
- 18:12 UTC: failover policy attempted to route to pool-east-02 but rejected because route whitelist lacked an alternate model quantization mapping.
- 18:18 UTC: queued QPS grew, several large-token requests timed out at frontend causing customer-visible errors.
- 18:50 UTC: mitigation applied — manual circuit breaker engaged to divert traffic to a degraded-but-compatible quantized model and reduce max-seq-length for affected routes. Latency returned near baseline by 19:00 UTC.

Key root causes (hypothesis + evidence):
1) Hysteresis in autoscaler + image pull rate limiting: autoscaler created nodes but kubelet init failed on ~30% due to registry throttling. Evidence: node init logs, repeated CRI backoff entries.
2) GPU kernel stalls likely caused by memory fragmentation on hosts with long-running serving containers (fragmentation visible in nvidia-smi stats; cumulative fragmentation metrics high).
3) Routing policy rigidness — the routing table requires explicit compatible model variants to be declared for each fallback pool. When the primary pool degraded, there was no automated compatibility mapping and requests were rejected.
4) No per-pool circuit-breaker to fail fast: current system tries to absorb requests into a degraded pool, causing queueing and head-of-line blocking.

Customer impact:
- Affected ~12 routes (mostly medium-to-large enterprise customers on Dedicated).
- Error spikes and latency > 5s observed for ~47 minutes.
- No data exfiltration or model corruption detected.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident (notes):
- 18:25 UTC: scaled back incoming throughput for affected routes via rate-limit override in gateway to reduce queueing. Command: curl -X POST $GATEWAY/admin/ratelimit -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","limit":40}' (manual).
- 18:35 UTC: temporarily disabled long-sequence heavy requests for known noisy tenants via tenant-tag blocking.
- 18:50 UTC: executed manual circuit breaker script to mark pool-west-01 as UNHEALTHY and applied routing override to quantized-model-7b on pool-east-02; updated route mapping in config store.
- 19:00 UTC: monitoring confirmed SLO recovery; began gradual reenablement of throttled routes.
proposed-circuit-breaker-design:
Design goals:
- Fail fast for pools showing sustained latency/queueing to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Automatic detection + progressive fallback (closed -> open -> half-open semantics).
- Safe model compatibility mapping so fallback pools use a compatible quantized or smaller model variant.
- Allow operations to override via admin API and to inspect decision rationale in tracing.

Suggested state machine (per-pool):
- CLOSED: normal flow. Monitor moving-window metrics (latency_p95, inflight_requests, queue_length, kernel_preempt_count).
- PROBING: when latency_p95 > 2s for 2m AND inflight_requests > X (configurable), mark PROBING and divert Y% of new requests to fallback route for 30s to validate capacity.
- OPEN: if probe fails (fallback also shows degraded metrics) OR queue_length continues to rise for 5m, open CB and stop routing new non-critical/large-token requests to that pool. Continue to allow small probes (5% traffic).
- HALF-OPEN: after cooldown (configurable e.g., 5m) allow limited healthy probes; if they succeed, transition CLOSED; else OPEN.

Metric thresholds (initial recommendations):
- probe threshold: latency_p95 > 2s for 2m
- open threshold: queue_length > 200 OR sustained latency_p95 > 4s for 5m
- half-open probe slice: 5% of traffic, max 10 RPS per route

Fallback strategy (multi-stage):
1) Shift to compatible quantized model on alternate pool (pre-declared compatibility matrix in config).
2) If quantized variant unavailable, degrade max_sequence_length and return high-confidence early completions.
3) As last resort, return HTTP 503 with informative body indicating temporary capacity constraint and suggested retry-after header.

Routing compatibility mapping:
- add a declarative compatibility table: model-id -> [compatible_variants], with compatibility flags (response-shape, function-calling, embeddings-compat). Use this to automatically select fallback variants when routing off primary pool.

Runbook draft (playbook for oncall):
- Trigger conditions: pool-latency-95 alert OR pool-queue-length alert.
- Page SRE on-call, include pool-id and top-3 affected routes.
- Quick triage (first 5 minutes):
  * Run: curl $MONITOR/api/pools/$POOL/metrics | jq '.latency_p95, .queue_length, .inflight'
  * Check node health: kubectl get nodes -l pool=$POOL -o wide; kubectl describe node <node> to look for imagepull/CRI backoff.
  * Check GPU-level anomalies: ssh node -> nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,compute_mode --format=csv -l 1 -c 5
  * Check for registry errors: journalctl -u kubelet | grep -i 'imagepullbackoff' || check registry logs
- Mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) If image pull/backoff observed: manually restart kubelet on affected nodes after confirming registry status; coordinate with infra if registry quota is throttling. Command: sudo systemctl restart kubelet
  2) Engage CB in PROBING mode via admin API: curl -X POST $ADMIN/pools/$POOL/cb -d '{"state":"probing","slice":0.1}'
  3) If probing shows failure within 3m: escalate to OPEN, divert traffic: curl -X POST $ADMIN/routes/override -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","fallback":"quantized-7b","pool":"pool-east-02"}'
  4) Backfill with on-demand batch-processing for long-running jobs where possible (schedule to dedicated batch queue)
  5) If kernel preemption/memory-frag suspected: restart offending containers one-by-one and monitor fragmentation metrics; prefer draining node rather than killing all containers simultaneously.
- Post-incident: collect traces for 30 minutes around incident window and create a synthetic watch (cron) to run small probe every 60s against each pool and record latency_p50/p95/p99 and kernel_preempt_count; alert on trend anomalies.
observability-changes-needed:
- Expose per-pool circuit-breaker state in Grafana panels and traces.
- Add dedicated panel for kernel_preempt_count + memory_fragmentation_estimate (computed from GPU memory alloc/free churn).
- Create a synthetic probe job that verifies compatibility fallback returns identical schema and function-calling behavior; run every 30s per route.
- Alerting: add composite alerts that combine queue_length AND kernel_preempt_count to reduce noisy paging.

Open action items (owners & ETA):
- Add compatibility matrix & automated fallback selection (owner: Hannah Li, ETA: 2025-11-26)
- Prototype and unit-test CB state machine in staging (owner: Jordan Kim, ETA: 2025-11-18)
- Add registry retry/backoff telemetry to node init logs (owner: Miguel Alvarez, ETA: 2025-11-20)
- Small synthetic probe per-pool + dashboard (owner: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2025-11-14)
- Postmortem writeup for exec (owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 2025-11-21)

Notes / Loose thoughts:
- We should consider tenant-aware CB thresholds: e.g., platform-critical tenants have more aggressive failover to avoid SLA violations.
- Long-term: evaluate pre-warmed image caches in regions to reduce imagePull backoff during autoscale events.
- Possible kernel-level mitigation: periodically restart long-lived serving containers after X days to reduce fragmentation (heavy-handed but effective).

Appendix: useful commands and queries
- Pool metrics (Prometheus): curl -s "$PROM/api/v1/query?query=pool_latency_p95{pool=\"pool-west-01\"}"
- Node GPU stats (one-liner): for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=pool-west-01 -o name); do nodename=${n#node/}; ssh $nodename "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv"; done
- Engage CB Admin API (example): curl -X POST $ADMIN/pools/pool-west-01/cb -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"state":"open","reason":"manual - kernel stalls"}'

If you have additional telemetry to add or alternative fallback ideas, drop them below. This is still a working document — aim is to land a minimal safe CB + fallback in the next sprint and follow up with a full postmortem for the incident JIRA.

-- Priya (oncall)
